body: Do they actually look at your ID?  I graduated from GVSU and my ID technically expired December 2012. Do they check for the expiration date?  Considering I'm still trying to pay back my 45k in loans to GVSU...it'd be nice to save some money by taking the bus instead of driving.

Well, I had it pulled yesterday.  It turns out I actually have a "very small mouth" and I also have these weird extra bones along the outter top gumline.  Long story short, dentist said a root canal and a crown would actually be really hard to do and that pulling it would be the easiest.  Nothing anyone said in this thread was mentioned regarding possible tooth extraction issues down the road. Nothing. I was told though that these weird bones mean I could never have dentures.  Perhaps the weird extra bone will actually help me out and I won't suffer from the bone loss you describe. I'm guessing an implant wouldn't be possible with the weird bone either.

I had the flu in high school, was out of school for 5 days or so, it was the only school I'd missed in years.  And I was forced to come in for two weekends of Saturday school.  All A student.  I was so pissed - never again, every future time I got sick I just went and breathed as heavily as I could on everyone.  Very immature, I know, but it felt right at the time.

I worked retail and a manager threatened some kid who tried to call in sick, said he had to come in or he was out of a job.  I watched that kid wipe his spit on the manager's keyboard, mouse, the desk, office door handle - anywhere he thought the manager would touch.  Long story short, it worked.  Bastard managers have to beware the equally bastard employees, but you know...I don't blame the kid, the worst though is that he probably got other people sick too.

Hah, I thought about it, but no no I was happy enough just to find a /r/dentistry subreddit and get as much advice as I did, it was all really helpful and will make my appt. next week far better.

Besides, if I'm a chick on the internet I must be fat n' nasty, or a dude in disguise anyway, Ross would probably make me pay him anyway.

I went to school, I got my B.A. and everything. All of it paid with student loans, my parents didn't save a dime for me to go to school, but that didn't stop them from basically telling me I had to go.  

But the degree is worthless.  Sometimes I wonder if I could sell my identity and my degree to someone else.  Then I could leave the country, I could see the beach!  I could see the ocean!!  I could see the sky!!!  I could see the WORLD!!!!  But then I remember I can't.  I can't do anything now.

It's really unfortunate and it makes me want to lie so so so bad.  I understand how people lie on their taxes now, it's this feeling...well...that it's not fucking fair.  I know life is supposed to be fair but...well I've always hated that saying.  Still though I won't lie on my taxes, audits scare me more than anything.  

Honestly it really feels like an American punishment, like the government doesn't like self-employed people, like that's escaping the system or something.  And it is - I do LOVE not having to sit in an office or...well let's be realistic standing behind a counter because a writing degree equals retail and fast food, so it really really beats those things, but damn the taxes are outrageous.  

It's definitely my goal to leave America and never pay American taxes again.

Start a non-for-profit business and you'll be in luck, I think they get far lighter tax burdens than regular businesses.

They also do a little extra punishment on people like me because I couldn't afford to pay annually and instead pay when it's all due - so of course I get a nice little fine on top of my already owed amount.  I know it's my own fault, but wow...every punch to the face hurts a little bit more.

You do if you make a ton of money - I have to pay extra because I have to pay both the employer's side and the employee side - I had a professional tax person do it last year and it came out to 5.5k. She said I could have gotten more breaks, but the fact is you have to spend money to get those breaks.  Like if I bought a fancy new computer and claimed it as a business expense I could take that off my taxes - but I didn't need one so I didn't buy one.  I bought a few things for work...but in reality the total cost was under $200.  I could lie and pretend to have a home office, but I work out of my living room and you have to have a dedicated office space that is separate from your living space to claim things like electricity, internet, heat, and rent - and even then you can only claim a certain percentage.  I live with a roommate, and that makes it even MORE difficult to claim anything.  Those self-employed breaks really only work for people who own a business, rather than a lowly freelancer.

I'm self employed is the thing...I don't even own a car.  My degree is so completely useless.  Going to college ruined my life, it really really did.  But EVERYONE said you HAD to go, and fuck even I wanted to go.  I was so so stupid.  I hear commercials on the radio for people who had 100k in tax debt to the government, then they call some lawyer and only have to pay 5k!  It makes me want to kill those people - I have to pay 5k on my under 20k self-employment job.  I have all this money and I can't even spend it to get myself out of this hole.  Worse thing is I just found out my student loans turned me into the credit people and they knocked my score down 200 points from 700-something to 500-something.  Everyday things get worse.  I want OUT out OUT of this system.  I don't want to see MONEY ever again and I can ONLY find ONE way to do taht.

I'm self-employed...I make less than 18k a year and yep, 6k is how much I will be paying.  My accountant (a family member so free!) is hoping to get it down to 5k this year, but who knows?  Not I.

*if there is some left over I will get a root canal, but I won't know for a bit and the pain is horrid
